processing: Little is documented about this garden's own methods; as with most Assam black tea, the leaf is withered, rolled or cut, fully oxidised and fired. Visitors are also shown green tea making.
harvest_season: As elsewhere in Assam, picking runs from spring into autumn, and the second flush of about May and June is generally the most prized.
appearance_dry: Typically dark brown Assam leaf; the exact look depends on the grade.
appearance_liquor: Usually a deep reddish amber, as is typical of Assam black tea.
appearance_wet: Typically coppery brown, as with other Assam black teas.
taste_profile: No detailed tasting record exists for this garden; expect the malty, brisk, full-bodied cup typical of Assam.

brewing.notes: General Assam guidance: Western-style with water just off the boil, and milk if you like it.

vintage_note: No regular pattern is documented for Sapoi itself. Assam black tea is usually sold by the current year's flush and grade and is best drunk within a year or two.
description:
Sapoi is a tea estate near Dhekiajuli in Assam's Sonitpur district, close to the Brahmaputra. It is better known to travellers than to tea drinkers, because the estate also takes guests in bungalows among the tea.

Its land is put at 2,600 acres. Guests can pick leaf, tour the factory, taste and try making green tea themselves, which says more about the place than any description of its tea does.

There are few tasting notes for Sapoi. As with other Assam black teas, expect body and malt rather than delicacy, and brew it on the strong side if milk is going in.

If you come across a packet, ask for the grade and flush. Without them, the estate name alone tells you little about what is in the cup.
history: Sapoi is said to have been established in 1914, under British rule, and to have been run for several generations by the Kanoi family. These details come from travel writing rather than estate records, so treat them as approximate.
